From 370e19042fb8ac68109f8bdb0fdd8118baf39318 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dikshita Agarwal <dikshita.agarwal@oss.qualcomm.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Dec 2025 12:01:23 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] Revert "media: iris: Add sanity check for stop streaming"

This reverts commit ad699fa78b59241c9d71a8cafb51525f3dab04d4.

Revert the check that skipped stop_streaming when the instance was in
IRIS_INST_ERROR, as it caused multiple regressions:

1. Buffers were not returned to vb2 when the instance was already in
   error state, triggering warnings in the vb2 core because buffer
   completion was skipped.

2. If a session failed early (e.g. unsupported configuration), the
   instance transitioned to IRIS_INST_ERROR. When userspace attempted
   to stop streaming for cleanup, stop_streaming was skipped due to the
   added check, preventing proper teardown and leaving the firmware
   in an inconsistent state.

Fixes: ad699fa78b59 ("media: iris: Add sanity check for stop streaming")
Signed-off-by: Dikshita Agarwal <dikshita.agarwal@oss.qualcomm.com>
Reviewed-by: Vikash Garodia <vikash.garodia@oss.qualcomm.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Bryan O'Donoghue <bod@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil+cisco@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/media/platform/qcom/iris/iris_vb2.c b/drivers/media/platform/qcom/iris/iris_vb2.c
index db8768d8a8f6..139b821f7952 100644
--- a/drivers/media/platform/qcom/iris/iris_vb2.c
+++ b/drivers/media/platform/qcom/iris/iris_vb2.c
@@ -231,8 +231,6 @@ void iris_vb2_stop_streaming(struct vb2_queue *q)
 		return;
 
 	mutex_lock(&inst->lock);
-	if (inst->state == IRIS_INST_ERROR)
-		goto exit;
 
 	if (!V4L2_TYPE_IS_OUTPUT(q->type) &&
 	    !V4L2_TYPE_IS_CAPTURE(q->type))
@@ -243,10 +241,10 @@ void iris_vb2_stop_streaming(struct vb2_queue *q)
 		goto exit;
 
 exit:
-	if (ret) {
-		iris_helper_buffers_done(inst, q->type, VB2_BUF_STATE_ERROR);
+	iris_helper_buffers_done(inst, q->type, VB2_BUF_STATE_ERROR);
+	if (ret)
 		iris_inst_change_state(inst, IRIS_INST_ERROR);
-	}
+
 	mutex_unlock(&inst->lock);
 }
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch reverts a previous commit (ad699fa78b59) that introduced a check in `iris_vb2_stop_streaming()` to skip the stop streaming process when the instance was already in `IRIS_INST_ERROR` state. The reverted change caused two regressions: buffers were not returned to vb2 (triggering warnings), and session cleanup was incomplete, leaving firmware in an inconsistent state.

**Modifications in the file `drivers/media/platform/qcom/iris/iris_vb2.c`:**

1. **Removed the early exit for error state** – The line `if (inst->state == IRIS_INST_ERROR) goto exit;` is deleted. This ensures that `stop_streaming` always proceeds to release buffers and perform teardown, even if the instance is already in an error state.

2. **Restructured the cleanup logic** – The call to `iris_helper_buffers_done()` is moved outside the `if (ret)` block, so buffers are unconditionally completed with `VB2_BUF_STATE_ERROR`. The state transition to `IRIS_INST_ERROR` now occurs only when `ret` is non-zero (i.e., an error occurred during the streaming stop operation), rather than being tied to the buffer completion.

**Relationship between the changes:** Both changes work together to fix the regressions introduced by the previous commit. Removing the early exit ensures that buffer cleanup always happens, and moving `buffers_done` outside the conditional ensures buffers are returned regardless of `ret`. The conditional state change preserves error tracking only when a new error occurs during stop streaming, while allowing proper resource release even in the pre-existing error state.

Here is the commit message:
Revert "media: iris: Add sanity check for stop streaming"

This reverts commit ad699fa78b59241c9d71a8cafb51525f3dab04d4.

Revert the check that skipped stop_streaming when the instance was in
IRIS_INST_ERROR, as it caused multiple regressions:

1. Buffers were not returned to vb2 when the instance was already in
   error state, triggering warnings in the vb2 core because buffer
   completion was skipped.

2. If a session failed early (e.g. unsupported configuration), the
   instance transitioned to IRIS_INST_ERROR. When userspace attempted
   to stop streaming for cleanup, stop_streaming was skipped due to the
   added check, preventing proper teardown and leaving the firmware
   in an inconsistent state.

Fixes: ad699fa78b59 ("media: iris: Add sanity check for stop streaming")
Signed-off-by: Dikshita Agarwal <dikshita.agarwal@oss.qualcomm.com>
Reviewed-by: Vikash Garodia <vikash.garodia@oss.qualcomm.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Bryan O'Donoghue <bod@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil+cisco@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The previous commit added a check in `iris_vb2_stop_streaming()` to skip the entire stop streaming procedure when the instance state was `IRIS_INST_ERROR`. This incorrectly prevented buffer completion and teardown from occurring, leading to vb2 core warnings (buffers not returned) and an inconsistent firmware state due to missing cleanup steps. The proper behavior is to always run buffer completion and perform cleanup even in an error state, only transitioning to `IRIS_INST_ERROR` if a new error occurs during stop streaming.

Here is the patch:
 
 void iris_vb2_stop_streaming(struct vb2_queue *q)
 {
 	struct iris_inst *inst;
 	int ret = 0;
 
 	inst = vb2_get_drv_priv(q);
 
 	if (V4L2_TYPE_IS_CAPTURE(q->type) && inst->state == IRIS_INST_INIT)
 		return;
 
 	mutex_lock(&inst->lock);
-	if (inst->state == IRIS_INST_ERROR)
-		goto exit;
 
 	if (!V4L2_TYPE_IS_OUTPUT(q->type) &&
 	    !V4L2_TYPE_IS_CAPTURE(q->type))
 		goto exit;
 
 	ret = iris_session_streamoff(inst, q->type);
 	if (ret)
 		goto exit;
 
 exit:
-	if (ret) {
-		iris_helper_buffers_done(inst, q->type, VB2_BUF_STATE_ERROR);
+	iris_helper_buffers_done(inst, q->type, VB2_BUF_STATE_ERROR);
+	if (ret)
 		iris_inst_change_state(inst, IRIS_INST_ERROR);
-	}
+
 	mutex_unlock(&inst->lock);
 }
